# 6. Reducing the joint eraser to the twelve physical fields

So far, the nominal joint eraser uses one fixed enlarged family. Its lowering depth \(D_*\) is fixed independently of all variable inputs.

The NS lowering mechanism extends to the coupled equations, but two details matter: the quadratic sign and the magnetic commutator.

## 6.1 Signed quadratic generation

For single Fourier waves \(a,b\),
\[
\mathcal B(a,a)=\mathcal B(b,b)=0.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathcal B(a+b,a+b)
=\mathcal B(a,b)+\mathcal B(b,a),
\]
whereas
\[
\mathcal B(a-b,a-b)
=-\mathcal B(a,b)-\mathcal B(b,a).                                \tag{6.1}
\]
Thus the fixed Fourier certificates give both signs through distinct square carriers. Reversing the sign of a carrier alone would not reverse its quadratic drift.

## 6.2 One lowering cell

For a fixed catalogue field \(F\), use
\[
\zeta(t)=A\,p(t/\ell)F,\qquad
p(z)=z(1-z)(2z-1).
\]
It vanishes at the endpoints and has zero integral. If
\[
\alpha(t)=\int_0^tA\,p(s/\ell)\,ds,
\]
define
\[
Q=e^{-\alpha L_F},\qquad
\mathcal M=e^{-\alpha C_F}.
\]
Both return exactly to the identity at a complete cell endpoint.

For nominal force \(g_0+g_1\), output the lower-space force
\[
f_{\rm low}=\zeta_t-\nu\Delta\zeta+g_0.
\]
Carry a continuous corrector
\[
\theta_t=-\mathcal B(\zeta,\zeta)-g_1,\qquad \theta(0)=0,          \tag{6.2}
\]
and set
\[
u=\zeta+\theta+Q\widetilde u,\qquad B=\mathcal M b.
\]

The large derivative \(\theta_t\) cancels exactly in the transformed momentum equation.

Choose the rational amplitudes so that the quadratic **cell-average** mismatch is at most \(\delta_0\), and the cell width so that the within-cell primitive is also at most \(\delta_0\). Then
\[
\sup_t\|\theta(t)\|_{H^{12}}\le C\delta_0.                        \tag{6.3}
\]
The accumulated endpoint mismatch is bounded by
\[
\sum_I|I|\delta_0\le\delta_0,
\]
rather than by the number of cells times an unweighted endpoint error.

The velocity corrector at the final endpoint is small; it need not vanish exactly. Exact return applies to \(Q,\mathcal M\).

=\rho\mathcal M^{-1}\Delta\mathcal M b
-C_{\mathcal M^{-1}\theta+\mathcal M^{-1}Q\widetilde u}b
+\mathcal M^{-1}h_B.                                             \tag{6.4}
\]
